source.title: Evaluating Self-Supervised Learning via Risk Decomposition
source.authors: Yann Dubois; Tatsunori B. Hashimoto; Percy Liang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures probe and encoder generalization errors and tests how SSL design choices relate to those errors, using a different method and setting from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on generalization-error components and how they relate to SSL design choices. Values used only to select hyperparameters or describe figures are not separately extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study cites Neyshabur et al. (2015) on larger networks improving generalization, but its own results do not test any listed version. It measures SSL representation quality and downstream linear-probe risk components. Representation dimensionality is not network width past interpolation; ViTs versus ResNets is not convolutional versus fully connected training; pretraining-optimizer associations with probe generalization do not establish V4's optimizer comparison; and batch-size associations lack V5's fixed-epoch comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors identify representation usability and probe generalization as the primary error sources, with probe generalization now the largest for modern SSL. Some design choices trade these components against each other, affecting full- versus few-shot performance, while others improve both. The design-choice analyses are observational and do not establish causality.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes pretrained self-supervised vision encoders and downstream linear-probe risk components on ImageNet, rather than the claim versions’ supervised training recipes and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported probe-generalization findings vary with representation dimensionality, encoder family, and SSL pretraining optimizer. The study also says larger batch sizes can be beneficial, while its global linear analysis did not find a significant impact.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe generalization becomes the largest error component for modern SSL models; yearly-average analyses show similar trends.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-sample generalization of downstream linear probes is a major bottleneck for modern SSL vision representations on ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing representation dimensionality worsens probe generalization; the controlled log-dimensionality coefficient is 3.8, with p=2e-9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing SSL representation dimensionality can worsen downstream linear-probe generalization while improving representation usability.

fits_no_version.finding: ViTs have better probe generalization than ResNets in the global linear analysis, and Adam/AdamW pretraining is associated with better probe generalization in SHAP analyses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSL encoder architecture and pretraining optimizer are associated with downstream linear-probe generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: SHAP analysis suggests benefits from larger pretraining batches, but the global linear analysis finds no significant impact.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Evidence for associations between SSL pretraining batch size and downstream risk components depends on the analysis method.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: Only 14 encoders were pretrained by the authors, so they note possible selection bias. Hyperparameter analyses are observational and do not imply causality. The authors report limited coverage and statistical power for controlled analysis, possible unconsidered confounders, and that XGBoost+SHAP cannot quantify statistical significance. The batch-size summary is qualitative and its global linear analysis did not find a significant impact.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were omitted. Figure-only values without textual attribution to a particular model or condition were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance under the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers trained from scratch, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under the stated tuning regimes, training-performance comparisons, and recovery strategies.
Large-batch held-out penalties at fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe adaptations remove them.
Dropout interventions across training-set sizes and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions, not denials of the reported SSL findings. No additional result bearing on V1–V8 was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same training recipes.
Width sweeps past zero training error in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch, and local-connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers’ held-out performance relative to their training performance under the specified tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to the training recipe.
Dropout’s effect on test error across training-set sizes and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: 169 pretrained SSL encoders (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained SSL encoders; downstream linear probing
rows.operation_detail: Measured probe generalization error as one component of an SSL risk decomposition.
rows.value: The study reports that probe generalization is now the largest source of error among the analyzed risk components for modern SSL.
rows.locator: Sections 5.1 and Summary and outlook; Figure 4
rows.note: Aggregate characterization; no single numeric error value is stated in the text.
rows.check: No listed version measures this decomposition. Figure 4 concerns the best ImageNet-pretrained model per publication year, rather than an aggregate of all 169 encoders; Appendix F.3 separately reports similar trends for yearly averages.

rows.subject: 169 pretrained SSL encoders (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained SSL encoders; downstream linear probing
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed association between representation dimensionality and probe generalization error.
rows.value: Increasing representation dimensionality worsens probe generalization error; the controlled-model coefficient for log dimensionality is 3.8 (CA: pvalue=2e-9).
rows.note: The finding concerns SSL representation dimensionality and downstream probe generalization, not network width past interpolation.
rows.check: The coefficient 3.8 and p-value 2e-9 are correctly reported, but concern representation dimensionality and probe generalization, not widening networks beyond zero training error. The controlled analysis uses eligible model comparisons, not necessarily all 169 encoders.

rows.subject: 169 pretrained SSL encoders (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained SSL encoders; downstream linear probing
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed association between encoder architecture family and probe generalization error.
rows.value: ViTs are significantly better than ResNets for probe generalization (GLA p-value = 9e-8).
rows.note: This is an encoder-family comparison in SSL, not a convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
rows.check: The reported GLA p-value is correct. SSL ViTs versus ResNets does not measure V3's convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch.

rows.subject: 169 pretrained SSL encoders (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained SSL encoders; downstream linear probing
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed association between SSL pretraining optimizer and probe generalization error.
rows.value: Adam and AdamW improve probe generalization.
rows.note: The result concerns the SSL encoder’s pretraining optimizer and a downstream probe’s generalization component.
rows.check: Appendix D.5 reports a suggestive observational association between SSL pretraining optimizers and downstream probe generalization. It does not provide V4's comparison under specified optimizer-tuning regimes; 'improve' should be qualified as an association.

rows.subject: 169 pretrained SSL encoders (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained SSL encoders; downstream linear probing
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed association between pretraining batch size and risk components.
rows.value: Larger batch sizes can be beneficial for all components, but the global linear analysis did not identify a significant impact.
rows.note: The text gives a qualified qualitative summary without a specific batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch result.
rows.check: The qualitative summary is accurate, including the nonsignificant global linear result. No specified small-versus-large batch comparison holds epochs fixed, so this cannot establish either the presence or absence of V5's penalty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
